title: Queue teardown and burst-control safeguards for hosted GPU pools
creator: Maya Chen
description: Summary: After the 2026-03-08 hosted API capacity event we observed long-lived queue amplification in several GPU pools that caused tenant unfairness and delayed autoscaling triggers. This ticket implements a two-part mitigation: (1) a graceful `queue teardown` mechanism that drains low-value pending work first while preserving in-flight generation and KV cache locality, and (2) a `burst-control` circuit-breaker that caps simultaneous pending request growth and degrades low-priority prefetch/warmup tasks under sustained pressure. The goal is to reduce queue tail latency, avoid cascading prewarm amplification, and ensure autoscaler signals reflect real compute need.
acceptance_criteria: Load test reproduces prior amplification scenario and new logic reduces 95th-percentile queue wait by >= 60%
No regression in median generation latency for P0 tenants (<= 5% increase vs baseline)
Heap of telemetry events (queue_age_histogram, pending_by_tenant, prefetch_drop_rate) ingested in Console; dashboards updated
Automated chaos test passes: simulated node loss + burst traffic results in soft teardown without >1% 5xx rate for high-SLA tenants
Rollout plan verified with canary + progressive ramp and clear rollback criteria

comments: 2026-03-10 Maya Chen: Incident triage concluded: burst came from simultaneous large-batch prewarm jobs plus an upstream dataset ingestion that created many long-tail KV cache entries. Initial hypothesis: prefetch weighting in the admission controller is too aggressive.

2026-03-11 Arjun Patel: Root cause update: found bug in prefetch scorer that ignored soft_capacity reservation for P0 tenants under certain concurrency patterns; this allowed many low-priority prefetches to occupy queue slots while autoscaler remained cold due to stale in-flight metrics.

2026-03-12 Nina Alvarez: Design review notes: prefer soft teardown (drain-by-score) over hard global drop to preserve SLA for in-flight requests. Circuit-breaker thresholds proposed: global_pending > 6x pool_capacity for 10s OR queue_growth_rate > 200% over 30s.

2026-03-13 Liam O'Connor: Telemetry plan attached; added new metrics and tagged events for tenant eviction decisions. Will surface in per-route dashboards and cost breakdown to analyze economic impact of drops.

2026-03-14 Priya Singh: Runbook draft submitted. Includes playbook for emergency fast-teardown (manual trigger) and steps for increasing capacity reservation for critical tenants. Need SRE review before merging.

2026-03-14 Sofia Martinez: QA created synthetic scenario that reproduces amplification with 85% fidelity. Tests currently failing on one timing edge (race between scheduler refresh and autoscaler scaling up) — flagged for fix.
2026-03-14 Marco Hernandez: Notified customer-ops for proactive comms in the event we need brief rate-limited rollout windows during canary. Preparing templated emails.
notes: Trade-offs: We accept small increases in warmup misses for low-priority tenants to protect high-SLA latency. Longer-term work (separate ticket) will revisit admission scoring using model-specific cost estimates and KV locality-aware packing.
next_steps: Finish code PRs, resolve QA timing race, run staging canary with 10% traffic for 24h, then 50% for 12h with SLO guardrails. Iterate thresholds based on observed queue_age_histogram and prefetch_drop_rate.
